review:
Let me preface this with the good parts of Bless.

It's fun. I genuinely have had a good enough time playing it, that if the developers actually treated their players like customers, I could recommend it right off the bat. However, that simply isn't the case. At all.

To begin with, the game is running on DX9 (mainly due to it using UE3) only at the time of this writing, meaning that it runs like crap for a lot of people, and simply ok for the majority of others. This makes zero sense when the developer has claimed they were going to optimize the game when bringing it to the West, and yet....haven't optimized really anything at all. And this is more apparent with the fact that the game as of now, has no hardware detection built into it. You have to go into the .ini files to edit things like your CPU and do simple things like uncap the FPS, just to get it to a state that's acceptable for most people.

The text translations for everything related to your skills is so bad that myself and my girlfriend just stared at the skill tree trying to figure out what we were supposed to be leveling up, and what each of them even did. This shoddy translation goes to the tutorial, and throughout the entire game as well. You even see placeholder level up text telling you "you've reached 2Level"....it's bad.

The game is censored so that NeoWiz could get a T rating and because of "local laws" in the regions they're releasing it. Which is one of the dumbest things I've heard considering the game is niche, the game is marketed to adults, tons of games on Steam have full nudity or sex scenes, the list goes on. It seems like this is another case of pandering where devs don't want anyone to be mad that there might be some nipples in a game. Oh, and they never said this upfront, people had to discover it themselves. 

The founder's pack items are character locked. I bought a Deluxe Edition for myself, made my first character, and had to delete it because of servers being so packed I was waiting 2 hours to get in. So I made a new character....and ALL of my Deluxe Edition items are gone. I sent in a support ticket on their site, which they closed and sent me a survey. No one responded whatsoever, and the devs on the forums are saying they're only looking into the Lumena being missing. Meaning all of the skins and pets, mounts, etc....gone. Thanks NeoWiz!!

The action combat for every class but Berserker has been disabled. And the devs have said on the forums they MAY re-enable it at some point. You know how action combat was one of the focal points of bringing it to the West? How they said they were fixing the combat and making it better? Me too....and then they pull this, again, without telling anyone prior to taking their money. People had to discover it.

Lastly, the developers are locking and deleting all topics that people create to simply bring up their practices. I myself have even received a warning for "creating drama" when I simply said that treating your customers like this will result in your game being ripped apart in reviews. Gamers aren't exactly the most forgiving, especially when it comes to their money being taken and being lied to.

It's sad, because in spite of ALL of these things, the game is actually enjoyable. I could see myself playing this as my main MMO, I could see myself spending more money on it, etc. However, with the treatment of the public by the developers, the lies, the underhanded censorship, and how every response from them is either one sentence long, or they just ignore it and delete it....I can't and won't be recommending this game to anyone right now.

Server issues happen at every MMO launch, game crashes happen, bugs happen....hell, I can forgive all of these things. But the lies and ridiculously poor treatment of paying customers is something that I refuse to just suck up and accept.

I understand this is Early Access, and they have promised to fix things. So, if they do indeed fix things as promised, and start treating the community like they matter, I will change and rewrite my review to a positive one. As of right now though, I would stay away. If you do decide to jump in early, at least you know what you're walking into.

Let me preface this review by stating that I played the JP version of Bless for a few months before buying in to the NA/EU release.  Seeing how NEOWIZ was taking the reins on their own product to self publish had me very hopeful that they would make a sincere effort to improve their game.  Combining the introduction of emissaries and NEOWIZ’s posts on needing us to play their game to get feedback on how to improve, this formulae gave a lot of players hope for this game.  However, as I write this review, those hopes were in vain.

Launch week went just like I was expecting, lots of crashes and issues that needed to be addressed, and that was fine.  NEOWIZ was actually reactive with the issues being posted in the steam discussions and proactive with changes and patch notes daily.  The first week, transparency and communications were there.  They were doing what they were supposed to be doing and I commended and defended them for it.  After that first week went by, that’s when feelings of animosity started to build within the community that supported this game.

After the first week, issues stopped being addressed.  Patch notes were just copy-pasta garbage and announcements to new unwanted content were being posted.  Sure, everyone wants to see new content being added but at least address the glaring issues being provided by the community playing your game first.  I’m not saying that they have to be fixed but at least address them.  It started to become painfully obvious that we were being ignored and that was the signature red flag that we’ve been duped.

It’s been 2 weeks since the last meaningful game balancing patch (1.0.0.8) and still nothing has been posted with regards to game balance or needed changes.  Sure there was the producer’s letter but I know a damage control PR fluff post when I see one.  I think the producer’s letter was the slap in the face that turned a lot of hopeful players off to Bless.  It’s my honest opinion that this was indeed a cash grab scam.

I say this is a scam because they hyped the game up as much as they could with announcements and an event.  They increased the hype factor via enthusiastic emissaries and used them hype it up even more on youtube and twitch.  On headstart launch they had close to 40k in game and the $150 package was #1 on steam sales.  All they had to do to maximizes profits was to be reactive, proactive and transparent for a week … and they did.  The week passed and steam wouldn’t allow refunds or chargebacks.  Coincidental or not, NEOWIZ was no longer reactive, proactive or transparent.  I can only see one obvious conclusion.

I cannot recommend this game to anyone.  The speculation and opinions discussed are my views so take it with a grain of salt.  Thank you for taking the time to read my review.

-zeiroe

[b]EDIT: Neowiz recently released a large patch as well as a new Producer's Letter that addresses/fixes SOME of the issues I bring up in this review. Most of the problems still exist and I can't recommend you spend your money on the game yet, but I'll edit the review to reflect the changes. My best advice at this time is to check on the game again in 2 months.[/b]

Hot Garbage Online should be the name of this one. I even have an extra copy of the game sitting in my inventory, but I'll never give it out because allowing another human being to "experience" this dumpster fire is too cruel for even me.

PROS:
-The mount and pet taming system is kind of cool.
-That's it.
-Literally that one thing.

CONS (wall of text warning):

- The "new" combat system is terrible. Every class is locked behind the same couple of combos, meaning you'll play your class exactly the same as every other idiot still playing this game.

- [strike]HUGE class imbalances in PVE and ESPECIALLY PVP. One Paladin is a god, two Paladins are immortal.[/strike][b]Paladins had their CC nerfed, but also received a 30% damage buff. Still not balanced, but at least they're trying new things.[/b]

-There are a lot of secondary stats in the game, but its completely pointless to stack any of them because the returns are awful. That means there is no room for creative builds, everyone just stacks base damage and health. Boring.

- Broken Battleground queues. Sometimes you'll get matched up against 5 players while you have a full team, and vice versa. Other times, the queue will never pop. Or you'll get matched against a 15-man premade with a bunch of solo players on your team.

- [strike]GUARANTEED to break ALL of your runes on EVERY PVE death. This includes the Ogres that are in the PVP BATTLEGROUND for one week each month.[/strike][b] This was changed to a 10% chance to break all of your runes on a PVE death, rather than a guarantee. I still think it's silly for all of your runes to break at the same time, regardless of the chances.[/b]

- [strike]Forced to grind a dungeon 8 levels lower than the max level HUNDREDS OF TIMES just to get the STARTER SET with decent rune slots.
--- OH, the whole set doesn't even drop. You have to craft the chestpiece. BUT WAIT, you CAN'T craft the chestpiece because the crafting mat was removed from the loot table LMAO!

- The only other set that exists in-game has an abysmal chance of dropping ONE piece from the final boss of the final dungeon. Someone on Reddit did the math, it will take you 1 whole year to finish the set with current drop rates assuming you're finishing all your runs each day.[/strike][b] They finally added crafting mats to the drop table, which means you can craft the level 37 chestpiece as well as the level 45 Epic gear. It also seems they buffed the drop rate of the Epic gear, AND they added Epic weapons. Good job, Neowiz. [/b]

-World bosses are pointless. They're far too strong for current gear levels, and have a TINY chance of dropping ONE piece of jewelry that gives a bonus to Energy, even though the Energy system was completely removed for the NA/EU version LOL
---And the geniuses even added a new one with todays patch HAHAHA

- The economy is stale, there is no efficient way to make gold that is widely known, so anything you list on the auction house sits there for a very long time without selling. Price restrictions similar to BDO prevent undercutting, [strike]and the minimum listing price increases each day. Everything is literally getting more expensive as time goes on, but there isn't a way to make enough gold to pay for it.[/strike] Crafting is also a grind and requires hours each day to make enough consumables to supply yourself for a few hours of actual gameplay.
[b] They significantly reduced the base price of most items you can list in the marketplace to reasonable levels, which helps the economy a lot. Too early to tell if these prices will rise over time like they did before.[/b]

- Artificial grind and content-gating. There is a LOT of content in the KR/JP versions of the game that are complete and working, and have been there for a long time. There is absolutely no reason to hold this content back from NA/EU unless they don't actually plan on developing new content and need to gate it to artificially extend the life of the game.

- No shared storage space across characters, and what you do have is tiny. This eventually forces you to buy inventory expansions, which are ABSURDLY expensive. Even if you buy the $200 Lumena pack, each inventory expansion will cost you close to $10, so you'll have to pony up about $100 PER CHARACTER to fully unlock your inventory.

- Cash shop currency is bound to the character you buy it on, not shared across your account. If you buy a big Lumena pack, you better really love that character because you can't use any of it for your others.

- Huge optimization issues. A fresh install of the game will net you a choppy 30 fps at most, you'll have to edit your .ini files and NVIDIA Control Panel settings if you want the game to run smoothly. Editing .ini files is at least pretty simple, but that raises the question of WHY THE FUCK CAN'T THE DEVS DO THIS THEMSELVES? ARE THEY REALLY THAT LAZY/INCOMPETENT? THE COMMUNITY SHOULDN'T HAVE TO FIX YOUR GAME FOR YOU!

- Translations brought to you by Google Translate. Incorrect tooltips and spelling errors everywhere.

- [strike]Too many servers, not enough players. Two weeks after launch and the game feels very empty, and it's getting worse by the day with no server merges in sight.[/strike][b] Neowiz announced server merges coming within the next two weeks, reducing the NA and EU server count down to 2 servers per region. This should make the game feel, well, not dead.[/b]

- No permabans for duping exploiters, just a slap on the wrist while many of them got to keep their ill-gotten gains.

- Virtually no communication from the Devs or CM's. No official forums, just the Reddit and the Discord. The CM's actively dodge questions on Discord and seem to enjoy trolling what remains of their playerbase.





     I'm sure theres many more cons that I forgot about, but I really don't care anymore and I'm getting tired. If you want to know more just go to Twitch/YouTube/Reddit and look for yourself. I really wanted to like this game since it's the only "new" MMO right now and we'll have to wait quite awhile for the next one, but I've run out of patience and hope.

Me: Max lvl (45) Guardian with highest gathering, mining, and armorsmithing you can realistically get at the moment with a gearscore of 7k+.

Combat:
 Not the most exciting combat, but not the worst. Each class has 4 availible stances, 2 you can use at one time and switch between giving you a fair amount of skills to play with..or so it seems. Many of the skills are highly niche and are never used, meaning that most classes have a boring rotation that works 95% of the time, and many skills are re-used in multiple trees with slightly different effects. Stance changing gives buffs, but for some classes its overlycomplicated, and for others they only add to the rigid best damage rotation. Combat becomes quite dull once you understand all your skills and realize the above. At this point all classes but zerker are tab targetting, but the zerker has numerous issues relating to the action combat style. Plans for action combat for all classes is promised, but at this point is nowhere in sight.

Gathering:
Everybody has a gathering, mining, and taming stat that levels as you do it. Subscribers get 30 day gathering tools, which otherwise you must stockpile in your inventory, Very generic gathering,  you see a shimmering bush, or ore and you gather it if you have the tool. Currently very little divesity in gatherable items.  

Crafting:
Crafting is just as generic. You can be an armorsmith(armor  + repair kits) , enchanter, (taming scrolls and spirits(runes)) or handicrafter (rings,  necklace, and bracers-bracers are NOT in game currently)  You go to a workbench in your capital with your gathered goods and just refine for 99% of the time. I got armorsmithing to master level by just smelting iron ore, making repair kits, and cloth. Never once made an actual item in the game, and never needed to. End game crafting requires you to run the dungeon that drops the exact same gear your looking to make, in hopes the last boss drops the rare crafting part. At this point in time to get above master level you must run the lvl 43 dungeon which is INCREDIBLY punishing and unfinishable by regular players. 

Secoundary crafting:
Pick from Cooking or Alchemy. Cooking gives you food that gives very underwhelming buffs, or food that boosts hp recovery out of combat. The second being the better item most of the time. Alchemy gives potions and gadgets, Both are very slow to level, and end game items require things most people cannot get.


PvP:
When lvl 35+ you are auto flagged for open world pvp unless you use an item to turn it off for 10 minutes, When you reach lvl 45 that item is ONLY buyable with lumina their premium currency. Those items don't matter too much, it just helps people quest, but at the same time this game would be MUCH better without it. The open world pvp was fun, but with the barrage of extreme balances that are not tested before going live, the game leans heavily in favor of certain classes. Curently palidins and mages are extremely strong. The recently released PvP instance 15v15 is okay but is riddled with things that make you ask..."why?". It is essentially capture and hold the flag to gain points, earn x points your team wins. The map has multiple PvE Ogres who not only can 2-3 shot a tank guardian and 1 shot squishier classes, and are also UNKILLABLE. They guard paths going to each point and the middle, and in the mess of fighting another person one can just walk up and insta kill you which leads to the next bad part. Spirits which are essentially enchantments for wow players, or crystals for bdo players that have a 100% breaking rate upon death and are not cheap. PvP also has no reduced durability loss, so it is very likely you will have a fully broken set of gear if your team is losing with no way to repair it there unless you have repair kits on you.  This mode would be fun if victory didnt come down to which team still has spirits, durability when it doesn't already come down to team composition. Other team may have 4 palidins while yours has one, and that right there can break the match.

Optimization:
This game is cluncky. It is not optimized, and while sometimes plays alright, the best you will get is alright. Going into your capital city will make you want to consider just closing it. I overlooked the performance for a long time, but it is not worth looking over. The game simply is not smooth and does not play well, as pointed out by the community in game every few minutes. You can play this game on low or ultra graphics and it plays the exact same level of clunckiness.

Trading / Player economy:
Auction house is slow, unresponsive, and for MANY people simply does not open for them. Personally I have to open it 3 times and close it each time, then re-open it to actually get it to load properly. The AH is designed after BDO's fixed price parameters. While its not an RNG market like BDO it means you have pretty much 0 control over how you price things. The market looks like this : Item A which is in demand = always highest price / non-existant on AH, Item B which isnt in demand = always lowest price/ flooded market. If you were hoping to play the market game, there isn't one. If you were hoping you could be a gatherer and sell your materials for some decent money, forget it, most gathered items aren't worth much, even the "rare" gathered materials won't net you much. The thing that makes the most money is the "Pet skill change scrolls" which you can buy with premium/ make in a few ways but it takes time going for 60+ gold. Level 45 blue quality +10 gear only goes for 10-30g at most. There is also no way of seeing some stats on the AH for things like accessories, so its a gamble till you find which ones actually benefit you.

Dungeons Que: 
There is 0 way to tell if you are getting close to finding a group. No estimated time, no ability to see who you've found for your group so far, no nothing. This wouldn't be so bad if you could get teleported to the dungeon, but no that costs 75 lumena (premium currency).  If you are half way around the world when your que pops you have to fly/run to the dungeon which can take quite awhile, risking you getting kicked from party, or party members leaving waiting for everybody to arrive. It also feels like re-queuing to replace a party member has no priority over regular ques and takes forever- if it is a healer you might as well disband.

Exploiters: 
This game has 3 other versions that have been out for quite awhile, while not the exact same, they share many similarities like the quests, leveling, areas, ect. There are exploits every few days in this game which occured in the other versions also. How and why these got overlooked is beyond me, and the punishment to said exploiters have up untill now been a slap on the wrist. Today they dealt with an exploit that allowed people to gather chili's the more expensive cooking material in abundance in a zone with nothing there but chilis and issued bans and warnings while taking away the chilis and gold equivilent. While their team seems like they are slowly getting more stern handed with exploiters, things like the duplication bug, was dealt with warnings and a max penalty of a 15 day suspension while in nearly all other mmos abusing a duplication bug on purpose would almost always result in permanent ban. I get the sense they are scared to issue bans as their playerbase is rapidly shrinking.

Things that irk me:

-Bank storage is 48 slots, not able to increase it at all. Not even enough to store profession items let alone other stuff.
-If you dont go armorsmithing and use the games blacksmiths to repair your max durability goes down each time.
-Quest log randomly only tracks one quest at a time and hides all others.
-LOTS of urgen maintenece with little notice.
-They have no test server.

Verdict: May be good in 3+ months, needs a lot of work. Don't invest your time at this moment.

I don't need to write an extensive review for this game.  It's shortcomings have been covered ad-nauseum a thousand different ways, so I'll just summarize here:

Pros:  The game -looked- good at pre launch...they knew how to make a decent cutscene.

Cons: 
  1. Poorly Optimized:  The game will crash at the slightest provocation.  It took hours of fiddling with settings to even make it playable.
 2. Horrible translations:  A 5 year old kid could write better sentence structure than some of the VOICED DIALOGUE in this game.  Anything great about the story is lost to this issue, and what can be deciphered in the illiterate mess is disjointed at best and utter verbal diharria at worst. 
3. No innovation:  This is an MMO at it's most basic.  Nothing new here. 
4. 30 levels of teasing:  The game is almost fun for just long enough to give you hope, then you hit endgame.  Dungeons leading up to the PVP zones are laughably easy, only to find any edits you put into your gear aren't permanent and can break anytime you die, PVP or otherwise.  There is no progression, only money.  
5.  Buggier than the underside of a 40 year old trailer left to rust in a swamp. (Not even exaggerating.  The game has so many bugs that if you ran a lice comb over it, you would probably lose your lunch you ate last week after one look at what came out.
      a. Auction house/item duplication bug:  Folks who took advantage of this one pre-server merge were able to make enough gold to literally destroy the entire in-game economy.  Especially with destroyable gear upgrates. 
      b.  Combat system: this is bbbrrrrooken.  For details, see the thousands of youtube videos.
      c. Early access my ass:  They released version 1.1, a finished game, a translated COPY of what was already released (and failed) in korea.  Then, the developers tried to justify it as being "unfinished," to try and excuse themselves for all the glaring issues.
      d. PVP queuing/balance:  Good luck getting into a match.  The machmaking was shit, and the actual battlegrounds lagged so badly on minimum potato settings on high end computers that any competetive aspect was swallowed in favor of whose computer would function the best so they could actually push their buttons.   That being said, when the system does work, the classes are horribly unbalanced.  Details of which can again be found in excruciating detail on youtube or forums. 
     e. Their debugging software will and has wrongfully flagged people who have not modded the game and permanently ban their accounts.  This issue is not fixed and developer responces are just "Talk to the provider, not our problem."  
 6. The utter ripping off of their "Patrons" and "Emessaries": The amount of rage felt in what passed for a "Community" in this game will be burning for years to come.  Streamers were allowed to play the finished version of the game pre-release, only to find no endgame content and no updates.  All bugs mentioned above and innumerable others existed, but were not corrected at all let alone in a timely fashion.  Which leads me to my final noteworthy point.

It goes without saying you will not get a refund if you purchased this game and discovered it's bugs more than 2 hours in.  Will not happen.  Unless, of course, you were a hacker who got your account banned, then steam will refund you as you can't play the game anymore.  Go figure.  Sucks for everyone who didn't actually break the ToU though. 

 7.  The most useless developers I have ever had the displeasure of speaking with and investigating.  These guys and their studio have released the EXACT SAME GAME no less than 4 times now, each time flopping worse than the last.  

Their community managers appear randomly chosen, are unpaid and generally don't really have a clue how to do their jobs.  They fulfill the role of constantly putting out community fires over outrage over this game, by offering new content people aren't even asking for. 

 Devs don't even review what players are complaining about and instead add a new patch every two weeks only to roll back (i am not exaggerating) 90% of the content they just added because it causes their servers to crash. 

Unfortuately, the negligence in game presentation and lack of actual new work going into the product has led me to believe their game is not only incomplete and downright awful, it's a scam.   Their arguably talented marketing team jumped on an economy desperate for the next great MMO, bled it dry of it's cash for early access content, and then laughed their way to the bank leaving Juuuust enough attention in place to act like they are still working on the game and avoid a lawsuit.  Trust me, it's not going to get any better.  The game has been out four years already, and has minimal support in it's home country, let alone here.  


All in all, this game is a train wreck that was transporting a dumpster fire to begin with.  Do not buy.  The most entertaining aspect of it was watching the forum and community servers on various media gripe and moan and yell at eachother for months straight, and watching the playerbase gradually tick down from 6 digit long numbers to five...and now four.  Soon to be three.  I shit the not, there are fewer than 2000 people still playing the game.  Worst $200 mistake I ever made.  And I'm an idiot.

This is going to be a long review. Don't read this if you don't have the time to read it.
I enjoy this game, I really do. The PvP combat is fun, the dungeons have moderately difficult boss mechanics to them and the revamped combat system is alright, but I can't recommend this game for people to play, not in its current state. The dev team is trying, but its like they're just throwing ideas and patches out at us without any testing, waiting to see how we react, and then acting accordingly based on how the population takes it. For a company that has launched this game in three other regions to be making such blatantly rookie mistakes over and over again is rough to watch. Lets get into the details.

Combat: This was super important for the new launch, and they did change things, turning it into a combo system over its previous incarnations. Its not finished though, it feels rough, like they didn't have any real testing done on the combat by real PvPers to format it accordingly. Some skills are locked behind combos in horrible places, like a ranger's silence. Some skill descriptions are broken, skills that should CC don't and skills that don't CC do. There's multiple, pointless animation locks without any way of breaking them to either dodge mechanics or evade an enemy player. It doesn't feel finished and it doesn't feel like it was tested at all.

Launch: Went back and forth on telling us 3 NA servers and 1, then launch day comes and there's one server, with the entire population under the belief its a megaserver. Suddenly they open up more, change their post under announcements(sorry guys no megaserver!), and now dozens of guilds end up split up across six different NA servers. Some completely rerolled off servers, others were unable to play with their guildies for days. Their idea of compensation? Here's some free lumena. The game constantly crashed which was expected, but it was also poorly optimized. Many people went into the config files to change things, discovering cheats and exploits to the game such as the dreaded "duping" bug which allowed people to endlessly copy items they had. Neowiz responded by handing out temporary bans to these players, but didn't take away the duped items for fear of it breaking the game's economy, so all of these cheaters remain far ahead of the average playerbase.

The game: A memory leak plagues quite a few players, and, as stated above, its pretty poorly optimized on DX9. My rig, while not new and sparkly, handles most games fairly well and it has a really rough time with Bless. The 43 and 45 dungeons, currently the highest easily accessible PvE content have no gear drops on any boss except the final, which has a very small drop chance. This means you can spend two hours in a dungeon, only to get a gold bar at the end(which equates to 1 gold for in-game currency.) Urutus Mine Elite, the other hard dungeon, currently does not spawn the last boss. (Haven't confirmed, will change if inaccurate.) The Bless team has stated they have no plans to change the drop rates for 43 and 45, thus leaving you able to waste several hours to gain nothing in the process. I want to preface this review with the acknowledgement that I understand this is an "early access" title -- I fully understand what that means, however, Bless Online was previously released in Korea, Japan, and Russia more than a year ago. So, while this is technically an "early access" game, it has an already established timeline and launch in other regions, which should be accounted for when reviewing the NA/EU iteration of the game. In these regions, the game was not received well and subsequently failed, being left with very small populations or being shut down. The biggest issues that Bless faced were dull combat, poor optimization, complete lack of content, and an aggressive cash shop. I will address these points in reviewing the NA/EU release of the game since NeoWiz has brought Bless to the Na/EU market with intentions to fix the previous problems Bless had in other regions. 

I will not be addressing launch-day related lag/server issues, as those are to be expected for a newly released MMO.

First and foremost, I have to say that the cash shop is much better than in previous versions. While I do not fully understand the intent behind some of the durability-repair items (which may be used for end-game enchanting), the cash shop does not appear to be P2W at all in my opinion. It offers some pet/mount skins, costumes, and some basic boosts that are fairly standard in most modern B2P/F2P MMOs (+EXP/Gold earned, etc). Also, you can convert in-game currency earned in PvP/dungeons into cash shop currency at a fairly decent rate, which makes anything purchasable from the cash shop earnable through in-game activities. You cannot convert cash shop currency to in-game currency. Cash shop purchased are charcater-bound only. Cash shop currency is also character-bound only.

While they seem to have held up their promise in keeping the cash shop free of P2W, the combat overhaul is half-finished at best and shoehorned in at worst. NeoWiz made it a point to showcase their changes to the dull combat system, however action combat is only enabled for one class currently (Berserker). The previous animations were never changed to work with a combo-based system. As a result, combat feels clunky and disconnected, since combos were added to classes with minimal change to how the skills interact; this leads to most skills simply being "deal X damage" with no interaction or intention behind their reason for being in a specific combo/stance. While this may change, only one of five classes has the "action combat" feature overhaul enabled. Furthermore, in other regions, there are a total of 8 classes; however, the NA/EU version on has 5. This give plays a very limited range of character classes to chose from, with only 1 tank class and 1 healer class. Currently, combat does not feel satisfying in my opinion.

Being brought to NA/EU, you would think that translation would have been the primary focus of the development team; however, while cutscenes have decent (at best) voice overs and translations, tooltips are lazily translated and are difficult to understand. Even the tutorial is a nightmare -- Within the first 10 minutes, you will be slapped with an impossible-to-discern tutorial on how to set up your combos/hotbars. In order to pass this portion, I had to turn to Google, Twitch, and YouTube to figure out how to continue through the tutorial (which is not skippable the first time you play, it seems). Tooltip translations for skills are completely botched, and it makes the confusing and convoltued combo system even less rewarding, as you truly will not understand what some skills do at all.

Performance issues that persisted in previous versions of Bless have also not been resolved at all. Bless utilizes the Unreal Engine 3 (which is fairly old at this point in time), and has all of the associated optimization issues typically associated with the engine. I have a fairly beefy gaming rig (980ti, 4790k, 16GM RAM, and SSD), and prior to tweaking the .ini files, I was lucky to get 30FPS even in solo instances. After tweaking with the .ini files, I was able to achieve decent performance (especially for a game that is several years old at this point); however, players should not be forced to dig around in .ini settings in order to get decent performance. Animations are also still very disjointed as they were in previous versions, which is made worse with the unfinished combo system.

Other issues I have with the game include: no player-to-player trading; poor (no) UI customization; no auto-loot function; no area-loot function; bottlenecked open world quests; camera position issues; no camer position customization options; over aggressive chat filters; and terrible default key bindings.

Right now, I would not recommend purchasing Bless Online due to these issues. Overall, I would give Bless Online a "playable game" out of "desert of MMO choices" rating -- In other words, a 4.5/10. If the above issues are addressed, I could see Bless Online becoming a decent game (7/10);however, until then, I do not recommend purchasing the game.

UPDATE: Turns out, there is currently no end-game content present in the core game. Fortunately, Neowiz did offer an apology after it was discovered, also acknowledging that there are serious duplication exploits present in the game (that were also present in the original game several years ago). I do give Neowiz props for admitting that the game is in a terrible state currently, and truly hope they quickly remedy the many problems facing the game. Bless Online was an ambitious fantasy MMORPG that aimed to deliver a massive persistent world filled with faction conflict, character progression, cooperative PvE, large-scale PvP, exploration, and creature taming. Developed by NEOWIZ BLESS STUDIO and published by NEOWIZ, the game had plenty of promising ideas and an impressive sense of scale. Unfortunately, its strongest concepts were frequently held back by technical problems, inconsistent combat, repetitive progression, and an overall lack of polish.

The world itself was one of the game's better qualities. Players traveled across large fantasy regions containing cities, settlements, forests, mountains, ruins, hostile territories, and areas belonging to rival factions. Environmental variety helped create a convincing sense of adventure, while the architecture and landscapes occasionally produced genuinely impressive scenery. Although some visual elements showed the limitations of the technology behind the game, the overall art direction gave the world a distinct high-fantasy atmosphere.

Character creation offered several races and classes, allowing players to establish different combat roles and identities. The broader conflict revolved around two major factions, Hieron and Union, providing a foundation for both the story and competitive multiplayer. This faction structure gave progression a larger context because players were not simply completing quests for personal rewards. They were also participating in a persistent rivalry that could eventually lead to confrontations with members of the opposing side.

Combat attempted to modernize the traditional MMORPG formula by incorporating faster attacks and combo-oriented mechanics. Classes offered different abilities and tactical responsibilities, particularly when playing with organized groups. Tanks, damage dealers, ranged fighters, and supporting characters could contribute differently depending on the encounter. Despite these ideas, combat was not consistently satisfying. Movement, targeting, animation transitions, and responsiveness sometimes lacked the smoothness necessary for an action-oriented system, making battles feel heavier or less precise than intended.

PvE progression followed a familiar structure. Players explored new areas, accepted quests, fought enemies, obtained equipment, improved their characters, and participated in increasingly challenging activities. Cooperative dungeons provided some of the better opportunities for teamwork, especially when encounters encouraged players to understand their class roles. Standard questing was considerably less memorable because many objectives relied on familiar routines involving defeating groups of enemies, gathering items, traveling between locations, and returning to NPCs. This made extended leveling sessions repetitive despite the size of the world.

Creature taming was among the more interesting features. Numerous creatures encountered throughout the world could potentially become useful companions, pets, or mounts. This encouraged players to pay attention to wildlife rather than treating every creature as another target. Hunting for unusual creatures added a collection-focused activity alongside ordinary questing and combat, giving explorers another reason to revisit different regions. It was a strong concept that could have become an even more important part of the game's identity with further refinement.

Large-scale PvP represented another major attraction. The rivalry between Hieron and Union supported open-world encounters and Realm versus Realm warfare involving substantial numbers of players. At its best, these battles created the impressive spectacle expected from a large MMORPG, with groups coordinating attacks and competing over objectives. Unfortunately, massive battles also highlighted performance limitations. Frame-rate problems, latency, optimization issues, and general instability could undermine encounters that were supposed to showcase the game at its most exciting.

Beyond combat, players could pursue equipment upgrades, mounts, pets, crafting-related progression, achievements, social activities, and other long-term objectives. These systems gave dedicated players multiple reasons to continue developing their characters. However, the experience struggled to establish a consistently rewarding progression loop because individual mechanics often felt less refined than their underlying concepts suggested.

Technical quality ultimately became one of the game's biggest problems. Optimization issues, bugs, server difficulties, interface frustrations, inconsistent responsiveness, and other rough edges affected the overall experience. These shortcomings were especially damaging for an MMORPG because stability and smooth performance are essential when dozens or potentially hundreds of players participate in the same activities. The game contained plenty of content, but quantity could not compensate for fundamental technical weaknesses.

Steam Deck compatibility is effectively unavailable in practical terms. Bless Online was created primarily as a Windows PC MMORPG and never developed into a meaningful officially supported Steam Deck experience. More importantly, the game's online service was permanently discontinued, meaning its original Steam version can no longer be played normally regardless of hardware. Even if compatibility tools could theoretically address some client-side issues, the absence of active official servers prevents normal gameplay.

Bless Online is ultimately remembered as an MMORPG with impressive ambitions but disappointing execution. Its attractive fantasy environments, extensive creature taming, faction-based warfare, class variety, cooperative content, and enormous PvP battles demonstrated considerable potential. Unfortunately, repetitive quest design, inconsistent combat, optimization problems, technical instability, and insufficient refinement prevented those elements from forming a truly compelling long-term experience.

There were worthwhile ideas beneath its problems, particularly for players who enjoyed expansive MMORPG worlds, collecting creatures, developing characters, and participating in faction warfare. Yet the gap between the game's ambitions and its actual execution remained too large. With the official service permanently closed, it now stands primarily as an interesting example of how enormous scope and promising systems cannot substitute for technical stability and polished gameplay.

No bald head options in character creation.

[i][b]Why do I like this game?[/b][/i]

Odd as it is:
[u]This game is inconvenient for most players who are looking for a smooth log-in have fun, log-out experience.[/u]
What that means is: There are no shortcuts. You cannot teleport around the map freely. There is not an easy party finder/dungeon teleport, you actually have to run to the dungeon you want to do. You need to run back to your corpse after dieing. Recent patches have nerfed the dmg so hard that some classes don't have it easy to just run around leveling solo.


[i][b]How can I like all these things without being called a masochist?[/b][/i]

Because it makes people in this game actually stick together. 
Having a hard time with your class means you need to party up and ask people if you want to go hunt together. What's the problem with that if you're playing an MMO?
There are different types of party buffs depending on the setup of your party from race to class. It supports variety and people teaming up.(Special buff for 5 mages etc.)
Crafting professions are limited to a character so in the long run you'll need a variety of players and you'll need to seek them out to get what you want.
You have to gather around the entrance of dungeons and try to recruit players. It keeps places busy and makes it not just an entrance you unlock once and afterwards you forget where the dungeon ever was.
Having no teleport options actually gives you a feeling of the entire map. Travel time matters, you appreciate the landscape design, again and again and sometimes find new things you didn't see before.
I'm tired of convenient quick-plays, dungeon finders, no interaction between players (I don't mean guilds, I mean the majority of the community) rushing content, teleporting and people just getting to max level and then spending 95% of their time in the main city because they can quickly access everything from there while the rest of the map dies out whilst screaming for new content.
There are many other things I could mention but I'll wrap it up there.


[i][b]Are these things super new and innovative?[/b][/i]

No. These ideas are actually old. We've seen them before. We've seen them in other games as well. But what makes this game worth playing for me is the way they gathered these ideas and put them all into one game. For the first time in a long while I feel like playing an old MMO, just with updated combat systems, mechanics, fresh graphics and a different setting and that's okay for me. 

If you don't like that, if you want the newest dynamic action-MMO with high-end effects and mindbending twists, convenient play, and have a smooth polished experienced served on your plate, this game just isn't for you. 
But if you enjoy investing time, teaming up with people and want a glimpse of the feeling you once had from MMOs like Vanilla WoW, a bit hard, a bit inconvenient but made worth by meeting people who're up for it struggle together with you, give it a try.

See: https://i.imgur.com/XHn0gH4.png

Lack of UI settings, screen resolution bug, and terrible default settings
It is not possible to change your screen resolution through the ingame settings without causing the game to freeze and blackscreen, which forces you to restart your PC. As of right now, the only way to safely change your ingame screen resolution is to directly edit the config files.

It is also not possible to customize the UI interface at all. You cannot resize core UI parts such as the chat or the mini-map. And there is a massive lack of game settings in general. Want to turn off the 60 FPS cap, increase your game FOV, or disable the inconsistent mouse smoothing? You have to manually modify the config files.

Terrible Optimization

Streamers opinon about the game (both streaming with 100k viewers at the time): https://clips.twitch.tv/BlatantFineFriesBCWarrior

Item Dupe Bug

Additionally, a lot of the attack animations lock you down in place so it does not feel fluid at all, and to make it even worse, some of the chain animations have a delay that makes it feel as if you are playing with 500ms.

Problems with potential future server merge / losing player names
Instead of adding shared servers and more channels, the developers decided to add 6 more servers on both NA and EU, which will become a huge problem in the future when the game's hype dies down. The servers will likely merge in an effort to boost player interaction, and some players will be forced to pick new player names (and maybe even lose their guild) due to them already being taken.

Excluding classes and content from the game on purpose
The game is missing the Assassin and Mystic and pretty much all of the endgame content that is present in other versions of the game, which the developers probably took out intentionally just so that they could gradually add the "new" content through the course of a couple of years without doing any real dev work.

And oddly enough, even though the Assassin class is not in the game, enemies still drop Assassin gear which is useless.

No Endgame - developers deceived players about there being one
The current version of the game, compared to the versions on RU and KR, is missing a lot of endgame features.

No Daily Dungeons
No Arenas or Battlegrounds
No PvP Ranking System
No PvP Reward System
Basel Canyon (main PvP map) is empty without mobs

Only two "end game" dungeons with exactly same gear score drops
SLEVELS (for unlocking last 2 stances and trait points) are not implemented, so you cannot progress past level 45.

The developers were quite deceiving about the lack of features as well -- selling founder packs and advertising a headstart as if there was an end to run to, plus falsely advertising about there being some end-game boss dungeons which are not present in the current version of the game.

Pay2Win, Overpriced Cash Shop, cash shop currency is CHARACTER bound
Cash shop currency is restricted to the specific character that you bought it on, rather than your entire account like in other MMOs, which is quite obnoxious.

And even though the game just came out and the developers claim a pure B2P, non-P2W marketing model, there are still a lot of convenience items in the cash shop, such as potions, experience and gold boosters, repair kits, resurrection scrolls, teleport scrolls, and even 20% dungeon point boosters. All of these items do give you a competitive advantage over other players even if only through faster progression, which I personally would consider P2W nonetheless.

On top of spending $30 for the game and an optional $15 sub, you still have to spend $20 on stuff like costumes, pet customes, pets, and mounts, or $15 to change your character's appearance.

This game is just one straightup money grab.

[u]Huge wall of text incoming, you've been warned.[/u]

[i]Bless is in a very interesting position. To my memory - this is the first MMO that community tries to kill, instead of game being killed by developer or publisher, like it happens with most other MMOs.[/i]

[h1]Let's start with negatives: [/h1]
[list]
[*]Translation could be better. Especially where skills are concerned. However it's one of those issues that can be fixed easily and fast and really not a big deal if you're playing the game at a normal pace.
[*]Optimization is pretty bad out of the box. It gets a lot better with certain tinkering in .ini files and your GPU driver control panel though. After some tinkering you'll get stable good peformance, I get 100+ fps in dungeons and 40+fps in very populated cities with GTX 970. If you're a PC gamer and don't know how to adjust your settings that's your own fault really, PC is not a console.
[*]Endgame PvP balance is meh. They're actively working on it though. 
[/list]
[h1]Moving on to UNDESERVED "negatives":[/h1]
[list]
[*]Launch experience is/was a lot better than a lot of people paint it out to be. At least in EU. The amount of time I have not been able to play the game due to maintenance in first 4 days sums up to around an hour and a half. (evening play sessions after work). This is the first time in my experience where additional servers got added almost instantly, closing registration/allowing it once again decisions were made promptly and the overall server performance was great except evening of 2nd day before server restart (physis btw). I've lived through a lot of MMO launches (LA2, WOW, Rift, GW, GW2, Wildstar, ESO, Archeage, BDO and many others) and this launch was decent. Don't even make me remember shit ESO pulled off with their "hey guys, EU servers will be located in NA until later this year BTW".
[*]"No endgame content" - Is just a pure lie. Yes, loot chances of highest tier gear in endgame dungeons are low. Gear still drops though, contrary to what a lot of people will make you believe. It's june 1st, less than a week since the pre-order start and they've already implemented the first battleground. Not to mention the glorious openworld RvR fights near dungeon entrances. There's plenty content, at least for now. 
[*]"Duping exploit" - stuff like this existed in EVERY eastern MMO upon it's launch in our region. We went through it with Tera, went through it with AA, went through it with BDO (well, BDO actually had plenty of game-breaking exploits not just on launch day but even months later, but that's a whole another matter). What's important is that issue has been quickly adressed, official stance on it was released, punishments were explained. 
[*]"Dated Graphics" are fine. Game isn't the most beautiful, but it's not ugly either. I can't criticize graphics.
[/list]
[h1]Positives :[/h1]
[list]
[*]There is NOTHING. And I mean NOTHING that can be considered "pay to win" in the cash-shop. Even the experience boost that is in the cash shop is so minor that having in-game pet with "xp" roll nets you 4x better bonus. 
[*]Vocal developer/publishing team that actually communicates with community. I CAN'T STRESS ENOUGH how important this is and what an impressive job they've done so far. A lot of the most annoying issues (like launch splash screen that they couldn't realistically test in dev environment because it was steam vs bless authentication issue) were solved in the first couple days. All of the major complaints get adressed in official news posts. Even if the game have released unfinished (which Early Access model suggests btw) - they're really doing a good job at fixing it and speaking with community. Battleground release in the first week of EA is something I didn't even expect, yet they're doing it. Server maintenance time were short (at  least during "normal" playing hours in EU region) and in-game server performance was top notch. Not to mention that they've still compensated all founders, and straight away claimed in developer letter that they will accept any refunds from people who didn't understand that they're buying into early access. Huge props for this.
[*]Combat in the game is probably one of the best adaptations of the "old classic mmo tab target". Somewhere around GW2. It starts off pretty weak, but at later levels combat system blossoms and even though it's still not "action combat" it's still satisfying, fun, impactful, and situation-dependant in terms of what skills and stances you have to equip.
[*]Voice acting is pretty good. Quality of VO recording is not stellar, but voice acting itself is good. Well done there. 
[*]Questing is your typical MMO questing. No grinding though. Not good, not bad. 
[*]Crafting and taming systems are "interesting enough". Not overcomplicated, but still rewarding for people who want to do that and not high-level-gated. Meaning that if you want to stay level 15 and make tons of gold with crafting - you can. Taming is very interesting as well.
[*]This one was a big one for me - ALL and I mean ALL of RNG chances are stated in game. You don't have to google/spreadsheet stuff in order to find out what are your chances of success(enchancement/pet upgrading), what is the boost from failstacking and so on. All of the percentages are clearly stated in the game client, so you don't have to do any guess-work. 
[*]Music in the game is pretty good. 
[*]Party content that exists. Decent but not stellar dungeons.  Interesting party-buff system (can be based on races, classes, a lot of different factors, and party leader selects the buff that will benefit party the most. "crafting parties" from random pick up groups have became very popular very fast. So a lot of people are socializing and talking to each other while doing crafting to get some sweet boosts).
[*]World lore/story actually has something behind it. 
[/list]
